static_traits.name: Chen Wei
static_traits.family_status: Living in a spacious home with spouse and daughters
static_traits.social_status: Has a supportive spouse with whom this problem can be discussed
static_traits.medical_history: No similar psychological problems before; never received psychotherapy; no significant physical illness
static_traits.language_features: Clear thinking, concrete expression, high cooperativeness, positive attitude, capable of self-reflection

basic_info.main_problem: I keep feeling frustrated with my rowing hobby. I often go out on windy days (I do not like wind), then focus only on the negative parts of those experiences, which affects my enjoyment of rowing.
basic_info.core_demands: I decided to seek counseling because this negative thinking and persistent frustration are affecting my overall enjoyment of the activities I love.

special_situations.event: When planning a rowing trip, encounters a windy weather forecast or strong wind that day
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If the weather is windy, this day will be ruined and the whole experience will be bad
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Changes travel dates and times, tries to choose calmer weather
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: This day will be terrible; my boating experience will be ruined by the wind again

special_situations.event: During sailing the wind rises and steering becomes difficult
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I cannot perform well on windy days, it shows I am clumsy / cannot do it
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Criticizing oneself with negative labels (such as 'I am so clumsy')
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I am just a clumsy person

special_situations.event: Recalling this sailing trip after returning to shore
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Negative experiences matter more; the positive parts do not count
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Focusing only on the details that went badly, ignoring any positive experiences
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: This time was utterly worthless; the next plan will be bad too

special_situations.event: Thinking that good weather is relatively rare, feeling worried about future outings
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Good weather is rare; I always run into windy days
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: At the planning stage, pessimistically evaluates the whole trip in advance
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I always run into windy days; it will always be like this

exception_events.target_problem: When planning or carrying out boating and encountering windy conditions, the client usually predicts the whole day will be bad and indulges in negative details, leading to frustration and reduced enjoyment, and continues to be irritable after returning home
exception_events.unique_outcome: On several outings, the wind noticeably weakened after a while, and the client did not keep dwelling on the negative as usual; the experience turned pleasant, feeling 'not bad' the whole day
exception_events.reason: Clue: wind weakened in the second half of the day (different situation); the client has years of rowing experience and skilled technique (supportive conditions), able to regain control and enjoy the activity when the wind weakened

positive_force: Loves rowing and goes out weekly
Having years of experience and high control skills
Has a supportive spouse to talk to and lean on
Willing to seek professional help with a positive attitude
Willing to check the weather forecast and adjust travel plans
negative_force: Tendency to catastrophize and predict the future (judging the whole day as bad at the sight of wind)
Mental filtering / dismissing positive experiences, focusing on negative details
Overgeneralization (generalizing one windy day into 'I always run into windy days')
Self-labeling and self-blame (attributing operational difficulties to 'I am clumsy')
Rumination and frustration spill over into family interactions

target_behavior.behavior: When sailing on a windy day, catastrophizing and persistent negative rumination, accompanied by strong frustration
antecedent: Seeing a windy forecast when planning to sail
Increasing wind and difficult handling during the voyage
target_behavior.core_reason: Negative cognition about windy days (predicting the whole day will be bad, ignoring the positive) and overgeneralizing momentary difficulty as personal inadequacy ('I am clumsy')
target_behavior.function: Emotional avoidance: lowers expectations and avoids disappointment through pessimistic evaluation in advance
target_behavior.consequence: Reduced enjoyment of rowing, low mood and irritability before and after outings

target_behavior.behavior: Spilling sense of frustration into family interactions (irritability / negative interactions with family)
antecedent: After sailing out on a windy day, still ruminates on negative experiences at home
target_behavior.core_reason: Not yet able to effectively regulate emotions and stop rumination; negative emotions accumulating
target_behavior.function: Vents negative emotions for brief relief
target_behavior.consequence: Affects interactions and atmosphere with spouse and family
